body:
# Ticket 1 — Claude accounts over the wire: list, remember, forget — Round 1

### Blocked by
—

### Description
The server can already remember, list and forget Claude accounts (`ClaudeAccounts` in `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts`), but no client can reach it. This ticket makes those three operations callable over T3's WebSocket RPC, from the web and desktop app, locally and remotely. It moves the account schemas and the account error into `packages/contracts` and rewrites every error message in plain words, with no internal setup ID and no command line in it. Later tickets build the screens on this.

No screen changes in this ticket. Switching (ticket 2) and adding an account (ticket 3) come later.

### Acceptance criteria
Scenario AK-14: Remembering the logged-in account from the Claude provider settings
  Given a Claude setup logged in with an account T3 has not remembered yet
  When the user chooses to remember it in the Claude provider settings and names it "Work"
  Then the account is remembered as "Work"
  And the settings list "Work" as the active account
Serves: R6

Scenario AK-25: Settings list the remembered accounts and mark the active one
  Given a Claude setup logged in as "Work" with "Work" and "Private" remembered
  When the user opens the Claude provider settings
  Then they see "Work" and "Private" listed
  And "Work" is marked as active
Serves: R10

Scenario AK-28: Confirming forget removes the account from the list
  Given the user has been asked to confirm forgetting "Private"
  When they confirm
  Then "Private" is no longer listed
  And "Private" is no longer offered for switching in the model picker
Serves: R10

Scenario AK-30: Forgetting the active account keeps the setup logged in
  Given a Claude setup logged in as the remembered account "Work"
  When the user forgets "Work" and confirms
  Then the setup is still logged in with that account
  And the account is shown as not remembered, with the offer to remember it
Serves: R10

Scenario AK-36: The desktop app connected remotely lists the remote setup's accounts
  Given the desktop app connected to a T3 on another machine whose Claude setup has "Work" active and "Private" remembered
  When the user opens the Claude provider settings
  Then they see "Work" and "Private" listed
  And "Work" is marked as active
Serves: R13

This ticket proves the server side of these scenarios, through the RPC boundary that a client uses. The screens that show the result, the confirmation dialogs and the offer to remember come in ticket 4 (settings) and ticket 5 (model picker). They consume the RPCs defined here.

### Test specification
Unit (`packages/contracts/src/claudeAccounts.test.ts`, new):
- For every literal in `ClaudeAccountErrorReason`, a `ClaudeAccountError` built with `instanceId: "claudeAgent_work"` and `name: "Work"` has a non-empty `message`. The message contains none of: `claudeAgent_work`, a backtick, `claude auth`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. (Proves the plain-language rule for every reason, including ones that tickets 2 and 3 will add.)
- A `ClaudeAccountError({ reason: "nameInUse", name: "Work" })` that is encoded with `Schema.encodeUnknownSync(ClaudeAccountError)` and decoded again with `Schema.decodeUnknownSync(ClaudeAccountError)` keeps its `reason`, its `name` and the same `message`. This shows the client rebuilds the same text.

Integration (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts`, new `describe("over the WebSocket RPC")` that reuses the file's existing harness: temp setup dirs, real `ServerSecretStore`, pinned `HostProcess`). The RPCs run through `RpcServer.makeNoSerialization` over `RpcGroup.make(WsClaudeAccountsListRpc, WsClaudeAccountsRememberRpc, WsClaudeAccountsForgetRpc)`, with handlers from `claudeAccountsRpcHandlers` and the real `ClaudeAccounts` layer, the same way `apps/server/src/ws.test.ts:602-631` drives Rpcs:
- AK-14: setup `claudeAgent` is logged in as an account that is not remembered. `claudeAccounts.remember { instanceId: "claudeAgent", name: "Work" }` returns `{ name: "Work", email }`. A following `claudeAccounts.list` shows the setup with `active.rememberedAs === "Work"`.
- AK-25 / AK-36: "Work" and "Private" are remembered and the setup is logged in as Work. `claudeAccounts.list` returns both names in `accounts`, and the setup's `active.rememberedAs` is `"Work"`.
- AK-28: after `claudeAccounts.forget { name: "Private" }`, `claudeAccounts.list` no longer contains "Private" in `accounts`.
- AK-30: after `claudeAccounts.forget { name: "Work" }` while Work is active, the setup's `.credentials.json` and `.claude.json` are byte-identical to before. `claudeAccounts.list` shows the setup with `active.email` unchanged and `active.rememberedAs === null`.
- A refused call reaches the caller as a typed failure. `claudeAccounts.remember` with a name already in use fails with `ClaudeAccountError` reason `nameInUse`, and its `message` contains no setup ID. With `HostProcess.Platform` set to `"darwin"`, `claudeAccounts.list` fails with reason `unavailable`.

Existing tests that must keep passing unchanged in their assertions: `apps/server/src/auth/RpcAuthorization.test.ts` (one scope per Rpc) and `apps/server/src/ws.test.ts` (it gains one `Layer.mock(ClaudeAccounts.ClaudeAccounts)({})` entry in its mock wall, because `layerWsRpc` now yields the service). The existing `ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts` assertions that pin the old `needsFreshLogin` and `switchRollbackFailed` texts (`:1374`, `:2214`) are updated to the new texts below. That is a required behaviour change (R11), and the hand-off must justify it.

Boundaries doubled: the Claude login check (`ClaudeLoginCheck`, already scripted in the harness), the `/proc` scan (fake proc root, already in the harness) and the host process (`HostProcess.*`, pinned). Everything else is real: secret store, settings service, SQLite in memory, the RPC server.

e2e: none. There is no e2e suite, and the integration tests above stand in for it. The screens are proven in tickets 4 and 5.

### Design reference


### Implementation details
Module: `packages/contracts` (wire types), `apps/server` (RPC handlers), `packages/client-runtime` (client atoms)

Files:
- [NEW] `packages/contracts/src/claudeAccounts.ts` — the Claude account wire types and error, moved from the server.
- [MODIFY] `packages/contracts/src/index.ts` — add `export * from "./claudeAccounts.ts";` next to `./providerSetup.ts`.
- [NEW] `packages/contracts/src/claudeAccounts.test.ts` — the unit tests above.
- [MODIFY] `packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts` — three `WS_METHODS` entries, three `Rpc.make` declarations, and their listing in `WsRpcGroup`.
- [MODIFY] `packages/contracts/src/clientRpcPermissions.ts` — guard remember and forget with `AuthProvidersManageScope`.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts` — delete the local schema and error definitions, import them from `@t3tools/contracts`, and re-export them, so existing imports of `./ClaudeAccounts.ts` keep working.
- [NEW] `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccountsRpc.ts` — the handler functions over the service.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/ws.ts` — yield the service in `layerWsRpc` and spread the handlers into `ServerWsRpcGroup.of({...})`.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/auth/RpcAuthorization.ts` — a required scope for the three methods.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/observability/RpcInstrumentation.ts` — span area `"provider"` for the three methods.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/ws.test.ts` — add `Layer.mock(ClaudeAccounts.ClaudeAccounts)({})` to the mock wall.
- [MODIFY] `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts` — the RPC describe block, and the two updated message assertions.
- [MODIFY] `packages/client-runtime/src/state/server.ts` — the client query and commands.

Consumes: nothing from earlier tickets. From the repository: `ClaudeAccounts` service (`remember`, `list`, `forget`), `ProviderInstanceId`, `EnvironmentAuthorizationError`, `AuthProvidersManageScope`, `AuthOrchestrationReadScope`.

Produces (exact names, used by tickets 2–6):
- In `@t3tools/contracts` (`claudeAccounts.ts`):
  - `ClaudeAccountErrorReason` — `Schema.Literals([...])` with the 17 existing reasons, unchanged in name and order.
  - `ClaudeAccountError` — `Schema.TaggedError<ClaudeAccountError>()("ClaudeAccountError", { reason: ClaudeAccountErrorReason, instanceId: Schema.optional(ProviderInstanceId), name: Schema.optional(Schema.String) })`, with the `message` getter below.
  - `RememberedClaudeAccount` — `Schema.Struct({ name: Schema.String, email: Schema.String })`.
  - `ClaudeSetupAccountState` — `Schema.Struct({ instanceId: ProviderInstanceId, displayName: Schema.NullOr(Schema.String), active: Schema.NullOr(Schema.Struct({ email: Schema.String, rememberedAs: Schema.NullOr(Schema.String) })) })`.
  - `ClaudeAccountList` — `Schema.Struct({ accounts: Schema.Array(RememberedClaudeAccount), setups: Schema.Array(ClaudeSetupAccountState) })`.
  - `ClaudeSwitchResult` — `Schema.Struct({ instanceId: ProviderInstanceId, active: RememberedClaudeAccount, affectedInstanceIds: Schema.Array(ProviderInstanceId) })`. It moves now, because it sits in the same block. Ticket 2 puts it on the wire.
  - `ClaudeAccountListInput` — `Schema.Struct({})`.
  - `ClaudeAccountRememberInput` — `Schema.Struct({ instanceId: ProviderInstanceId, name: Schema.String })`.
  - `ClaudeAccountForgetInput` — `Schema.Struct({ name: Schema.String })`.
  - Each schema also exports its `type X = typeof X.Type`, as the server file does today.
- In `packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts`:
  - `WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsList = "claudeAccounts.list"`, `WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsRemember = "claudeAccounts.remember"`, `WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsForget = "claudeAccounts.forget"`.
  - `ClaudeAccountRpcError = Schema.Union([ClaudeAccountError, EnvironmentAuthorizationError])`, exported for tickets 2 and 3.
  - `WsClaudeAccountsListRpc` (payload `ClaudeAccountListInput`, success `ClaudeAccountList`), `WsClaudeAccountsRememberRpc` (payload `ClaudeAccountRememberInput`, success `RememberedClaudeAccount`) and `WsClaudeAccountsForgetRpc` (payload `ClaudeAccountForgetInput`, success `Schema.Void`). All three use error `ClaudeAccountRpcError`, and all three are exported so the integration test can build its group.
- In `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccountsRpc.ts`: `export const claudeAccountsRpcHandlers = (accounts: ClaudeAccounts["Service"]) => ({ [WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsList]: (_input: ClaudeAccountListInput) => accounts.list, [WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsRemember]: (input: ClaudeAccountRememberInput) => accounts.remember(input), [WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsForget]: (input: ClaudeAccountForgetInput) => accounts.forget(input) })`. Tickets 2 and 3 add their handlers to this same object.
- In `packages/client-runtime/src/state/server.ts`, inside `createServerEnvironmentAtoms`:
  - `claudeAccountList: createEnvironmentRpcQueryAtomFamily(runtime, { label: "environment-data:claude-accounts:list", tag: WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsList })`.
  - `rememberClaudeAccount: createEnvironmentRpcCommand(runtime, { label: "environment-data:claude-accounts:remember", tag: WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsRemember })`.
  - `forgetClaudeAccount: createEnvironmentRpcCommand(runtime, { label: "environment-data:claude-accounts:forget", tag: WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsForget })`.
  - The web reads them as `serverEnvironment.claudeAccountList`, `serverEnvironment.rememberClaudeAccount` and `serverEnvironment.forgetClaudeAccount`, with targets `{ environmentId, input }`.

Scopes:
- `claudeAccountsList` → `AuthOrchestrationReadScope`. The same account email already reaches every reader through the provider snapshot (`ServerProviderAuth.email`), and the model picker must show the account to any session that can see the composer.
- `claudeAccountsRemember` and `claudeAccountsForget` → `AuthProvidersManageScope`, the scope of every other provider credential mutation (`providerAuthStart`, `providerAuthLogout`). Both are also listed in `CLIENT_GUARDED_RPC_SCOPES` as `[WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsRemember]: AuthProvidersManageScope` and `[WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsForget]: AuthProvidersManageScope`, so screens can read `serverEnvironment.rememberClaudeAccount.permissionAtom(environmentId)` (AGENTS.md rule for new guarded mutations).

Error messages: the `message` getter moves into contracts with these exact texts, each a JavaScript template where `${this.name}` appears:
- `unavailable`: "Switching Claude accounts is only supported when T3 runs on Linux."
- `setupNotFound`: "This Claude setup no longer exists."
- `setupUnreadable`: "T3 could not read the login of this Claude setup."
- `notLoggedIn`: "No Claude account is logged in on this Claude setup."
- `invalidName`: "An account name must be 1 to 64 characters long and contain no control characters." (unchanged)
- `nameInUse`: `The name "${this.name}" is already in use.` (unchanged)
- `alreadyRemembered`: `This account is already remembered as "${this.name}".` (unchanged)
- `accountNotFound`: `No remembered Claude account is named "${this.name}".` (unchanged)
- `storage`: "Could not read or save the remembered Claude accounts." (unchanged)
- `currentNotRemembered`: "The account logged in on this Claude setup is not remembered yet. Remember it first, then switch."
- `needsFreshLogin`: `The saved login of "${this.name}" no longer works. Forget "${this.name}", then add it again.`
- `loginCheckFailed`: `Could not check the saved login of "${this.name}". Try again.` (unchanged)
- `switchFailed`: "Switching failed. The Claude setup is still logged in as before."
- `switchRollbackFailed`: "Switching failed and the Claude setup's login could not be restored. Log in to this Claude setup again."
- `externalClaudePrograms`: "Claude programs started outside T3 are using this Claude setup. Close them, then switch again."
- `processCheckFailed`: "T3 could not check whether Claude programs started outside T3 are using this Claude setup. Try again."
- `sessionStopFailed`: "T3 could not stop the running turns on this Claude setup. It is still logged in as before. Try again."

`instanceId` stays a field on the error for logs and for clients that want to point at the setup. The text no longer contains it.

Decisions:
- Handlers live in a small `ClaudeAccountsRpc.ts` and are spread into `ws.ts`, instead of being written inline there. This lets the integration test drive the real handlers with the real service and the existing temp-dir harness, without building the whole `layerWsRpc` mock wall. The cost is that one area of handlers sits outside `ws.ts`. The handlers stay one-line delegations, as AGENTS.md:154 asks.
- The schemas move to contracts and are re-exported from `ClaudeAccounts.ts`, not duplicated. One definition crosses the wire, and the 2216-line integration test keeps its imports. The cost is a re-export line in the server module.
- The messages carry no setup ID. They say "this Claude setup", because every place that shows them (picker row, setup card, add dialog) already sits on one setup. The cost: a log line that only has the message loses the ID, but `instanceId` stays on the error and in the existing structured log fields.
- `needsFreshLogin` now points to the in-app way out (forget, then add again; adding comes in ticket 3) instead of a CLI command. The cost: until ticket 3 lands, that advice names a button that does not exist yet. Both tickets ship in the same Auftrag.

Handler wiring in `ws.ts`: at the top of `layerWsRpc`, next to `const providerAuth = yield* ProviderAuthService.ProviderAuthService;` (`apps/server/src/ws.ts:1279`), add `const claudeAccounts = yield* ClaudeAccounts.ClaudeAccounts;` (with `import * as ClaudeAccounts from "./provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts";` and `import { claudeAccountsRpcHandlers } from "./provider/ClaudeAccountsRpc.ts";`). Inside `ServerWsRpcGroup.of({...})` (`apps/server/src/ws.ts:1806`), add `...claudeAccountsRpcHandlers(claudeAccounts),`. No error mapping is needed, because the service already fails with the wire type `ClaudeAccountError`. No new layer wiring is needed, because `ClaudeAccounts` already reaches `layerWsRpc` through `layerProduction` (`apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/runtimeLayer.ts:396`).

Consumers updated by the contracts change: `apps/server` (handlers, scope map, instrumentation map) and `packages/client-runtime` (atoms). `apps/web`, `apps/desktop` and `apps/mobile` need no change: `RpcClient.make(WsRpcGroup)` picks up the new tags (`packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/protocol.ts:5`). The mobile app is out of scope and gets no screen.

Deliberately left out: the switch RPC (ticket 2), the add-account login (ticket 3), and every screen (tickets 4–6). There is no capability flag for "accounts supported" in `ExecutionEnvironmentCapabilities`. Clients gate on `ServerConfig.environment.platform.os === "linux"`, and the server refuses with `unavailable` anywhere else.

---
VERDICT: DRAFT

# Focus — Ticket 1: Claude accounts over the wire: list, remember, forget — Round 1

| Criterion | Requirement | Exists in Auftrag, text matches | What this ticket proves | End to end in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AK-14 | R6 (remember the unremembered account) | yes | remember RPC, then list shows `rememberedAs` | ticket 4 |
| AK-25 | R10 (list, mark active) | yes | list RPC returns both, active marked | ticket 4 |
| AK-28 | R10 (forget after confirm) | yes | forget RPC removes from list | ticket 4 (settings), ticket 5 (picker clause) |
| AK-30 | R10 (forget active keeps login) | yes | credential files byte-identical, `rememberedAs` null | ticket 4 |
| AK-36 | R13 (web/desktop, also remote) | yes | same list RPC as AK-25 | ticket 4 |
| — | R11 (refusals in plain words) | not cited | all 17 messages rewritten, unit-tested | — |

## Findings

**[suggestion] focus-1 — The message rewrite serves R11, but the ticket cites no R11 criterion**
**Where:** §Description, "rewrites every error message in plain words"; §Implementation details, "Error messages"
**Evidence:** Auftrag R11 ("When T3 refuses an action, the user sees the reason in plain words") and its criterion AK-31; the ticket names R11 only in §Test specification, "That is a required behaviour change (R11)"
**Why:** the largest behaviour change in the ticket is missing from its criteria list, so the Coverage check cannot see that R11's message rule lands here while AK-31 itself lands with the switch.
**Taken or declined when:** §Acceptance criteria names R11 as served by the message texts and says which ticket proves AK-31 end to end.

**[suggestion] focus-2 — AK-36's remote clause has no proof of its own**
**Where:** §Test specification, "AK-25 / AK-36"
**Evidence:** AK-36 "the desktop app connected to a T3 on another machine"; the test drives the same in-process RPC as AK-25
**Why:** the test proves the list, not the remote path, so AK-36 reads as covered here while its distinguishing clause is untested.
**Taken or declined when:** the ticket says AK-36 is proven here only as far as AK-25 is, and names the ticket that proves the remote connection.

## Out of lens
gremium-security: `claudeAccountsList` under `AuthOrchestrationReadScope` exposes remembered account names and emails to every reader; the ticket justifies it, the seat should weigh it.
0 blockers, 2 suggestions. The ticket traces to R6, R10 and R13 cleanly; it leaves R11 and the remote clause of AK-36 implicit.

# Pragmatist — Ticket 1: Claude accounts over the wire: list, remember, forget — Round 1

## Findings

**[blocker] pragmatist-1 — The message rewrite serves R11, whose criteria belong to tickets 2 and 3**
**Where:** ticket §Description, "rewrites every error message in plain words"; §Implementation details, "Error messages"; §Test specification, the two updated assertions at `:1374`, `:2214`
**Evidence:** R11 is served by AK-31 (refused switch) and AK-32 (refused add-account) in the Auftrag; this ticket lists neither. Seven of the rewritten reasons (`currentNotRemembered`, `needsFreshLogin`, `switchFailed`, `switchRollbackFailed`, `externalClaudePrograms`, `processCheckFailed`, `sessionStopFailed`) only arise on `switch`, which this ticket does not expose. §Decisions admits the new `needsFreshLogin` text names a button that does not exist yet.
**Why:** the switch-message change could be accepted or rejected on its own, and it changes existing switch-test assertions in a ticket about list, remember and forget.
**Closes when:** the ticket moves the error class with its current texts and rewrites only the reasons that `list`, `remember` and `forget` can return. The switch texts and the two assertion updates move to ticket 2 under AK-31. Alternatively, the ticket names the criterion of its own that requires the full rewrite.

**[suggestion] pragmatist-2 — `ClaudeSwitchResult` moves without a consumer in this ticket**
**Where:** §Produces, "It moves now, because it sits in the same block. Ticket 2 puts it on the wire."
**Evidence:** no RPC in this ticket returns it.
**Why:** ticket 2 needs it, so ticket 2 can move it with the switch RPC. That keeps this diff to what its criteria use.
**Taken or declined when:** the schema moves in ticket 2, or the ticket says why it must move now.

**[suggestion] pragmatist-3 — New guarded methods skip the permission behaviour tests that AGENTS.md asks for**
**Where:** §Implementation details, `clientRpcPermissions.ts` entry; §Test specification
**Evidence:** AGENTS.md:153: "extend the permission behavior tests when adding a protected method".
**Why:** the ticket follows half of the convention for guarded mutations and leaves the test half out without saying why.
**Taken or declined when:** the test specification names the permission test it extends, or says why none applies.
Round 1:  1 blockers, 2 suggestions. The message rewrite for switch errors serves R11, whose criteria belong to tickets 2 and 3, not this one.

# Solutions Architect — Ticket 1: Claude accounts over the wire: list, remember, forget — Round 1

## Findings

**[suggestion] architect-1 — The list query has no stated refresh path after remember or forget**
**Where:** ticket §Implementation details, Produces, `claudeAccountList: createEnvironmentRpcQueryAtomFamily(...)`
**Evidence:** fact #78, #115: query families cache per target; `createEnvironmentRpcQueryAtomFamily` takes `refreshTrigger`/`staleTimeMs` (packages/client-runtime/src/state/runtime.ts:752-780); the ticket sets neither, and AK-28 needs "Private is no longer listed"
**Why:** tickets 4 and 5 consume this atom by name; if it does not refresh after `rememberClaudeAccount`/`forgetClaudeAccount` (or after a switch in ticket 2), each screen will invent its own refresh and the contract tickets 4–5 build on is decided implicitly.
**Taken or declined when:** the ticket says how `claudeAccountList` is refreshed after its own mutations (refreshTrigger, explicit `refresh`, or left to the screens — stated).

**[suggestion] architect-2 — Client gating on `platform.os === "linux"` couples clients to a server implementation detail; the cost is not named**
**Where:** ticket §Implementation details, "Deliberately left out", the sentence "Clients gate on `ServerConfig.environment.platform.os === "linux"`"
**Evidence:** fact #72 (no capability flag exists, `ExecutionEnvironmentCapabilities` is where feature flags live), fact #73 (OS-gating precedent), fact #3 (Linux-only is a `requireLinux` check inside the service)
**Why:** the decision names no alternative and no cost: if the server ever lifts `requireLinux`, every client check has to change, whereas a capability flag would move with the server.
**Taken or declined when:** the decision names the capability-flag alternative and what the OS check gives up, or picks the flag.

**[suggestion] architect-3 — Two sources for "the active account" with no stated owner**
**Where:** ticket §Implementation details, Produces, `ClaudeSetupAccountState.active.email`; §Scopes, "The same account email already reaches every reader through the provider snapshot"
**Evidence:** fact #64 (snapshot `auth.email` is published and pushed via `providerStatuses`, fact #62); fact #9 (`list` computes `active` from the login files on each call)
**Why:** later tickets will show the active account from one of two places that can disagree (pushed, cached up to 5 min per fact #65, vs. pulled on demand); naming now which one screens read for "active" keeps tickets 4–5 from choosing differently.
**Taken or declined when:** the ticket states which of the two the screens treat as the active account, or defers it to ticket 4 explicitly.

## Out of lens
gremium-security: the RPC integration tests run a bare `RpcGroup.make(...)` via `makeNoSerialization` without `RpcScopeAuthorization`, so the chosen scopes are proven only by the map's completeness check, not by a refused call.
Round 1: 0 blockers, 3 suggestions. The produced client contract leaves refresh, platform gating and the source of the active account for later tickets to decide implicitly.

# Security — Ticket 1: Claude accounts over the wire: list, remember, forget — Round 1

## Findings

**[blocker] security-1 — `claudeAccounts.list` gives read-only sessions the email of every remembered account**
**Where:** ticket §Implementation details, Scopes, "`claudeAccountsList` → `AuthOrchestrationReadScope`. The same account email already reaches every reader…"
**Evidence:** fact #64: the provider snapshot publishes only the *active* login's email; fact #9 and #18: `list` returns all remembered accounts globally, each with `email`. `packages/contracts/src/auth.ts` lets a grant be narrowed to explicit scopes, so a session with `orchestration:read` and without `providers:manage` exists.
**Why:** the rationale is wrong for every non-active account: a narrowed read-only session newly learns the emails of all accounts the owner has remembered, across every setup — personal data moved to a wider audience without the ticket saying so.
**Closes when:** the ticket either puts `list` (or the `email` of non-active accounts) behind `AuthProvidersManageScope`, or names this exposure as a deliberate choice with a reason the Purpose supports, and the test specification proves whichever rule it picks.

**[blocker] security-2 — No test proves the scope of the three new methods**
**Where:** ticket §Test specification — the RPC tests run through `RpcServer.makeNoSerialization` without `RpcAuthorization`, and `RpcAuthorization.test.ts` stays "unchanged in its assertions"
**Evidence:** fact #44: that test only checks every Rpc has *some* scope; the same file already pins specific mappings per method (e.g. webhook delivery logs → operate, relay read vs write) with `requiredScopeForRpcMethod`.
**Why:** remember and forget mutate stored OAuth logins (fact #16); a mapping typed as `AuthOrchestrationReadScope` by mistake would compile, pass every listed test and let any reader forget accounts.
**Closes when:** the test specification adds assertions that remember and forget require `AuthProvidersManageScope` and list requires the scope security-1 settles on, in `RpcAuthorization.test.ts` alongside the existing per-method cases.

**[suggestion] security-3 — Assert that no login data crosses the RPC boundary**
**Where:** ticket §Test specification, Integration
**Evidence:** fact #53: the harness already has `assertNoLogin`; fact #17: tokens are `Redacted` in the service.
**Why:** the schemas now cross the wire for the first time; one cheap assertion over every RPC success and failure body proves no token or path leaks through encoding.
**Taken or declined when:** the ticket states whether the RPC describe block runs `assertNoLogin` over the encoded responses and errors.

**[suggestion] security-4 — Declare the remember/forget scopes once**
**Where:** ticket §Files, `RpcAuthorization.ts` "a required scope for the three methods", and §Scopes, `CLIENT_GUARDED_RPC_SCOPES`
**Evidence:** fact #47: `CLIENT_GUARDED_RPC_SCOPES` is spread into `RPC_REQUIRED_SCOPES`.
**Why:** writing remember and forget in both maps creates two copies of the same control that can drift; a later explicit key silently overrides the spread one.
**Taken or declined when:** the ticket says `RpcAuthorization.ts` gains only the `claudeAccountsList` entry.

**[suggestion] security-5 — Bound `name` in the wire schema**
**Where:** ticket §Produces, `ClaudeAccountRememberInput` and `ClaudeAccountForgetInput`, `name: Schema.String`
**Evidence:** fact #8: the service enforces 1–64 characters only after decoding.
**Why:** a length check at the schema refuses an oversized name at the RPC boundary before it reaches the service, its logs (fact #17 logs the name) or an error message that echoes it.
**Taken or declined when:** the ticket states whether the input schemas carry a maximum length.
Round 1:  2 blockers, 3 suggestions. The access rule for the new methods is wrong for list and proven for none.

# API contract — Ticket 1: Claude accounts over the wire: list, remember, forget — Round 1

## Findings

**[blocker] api-contract-1 — The error reason is a closed enum on the wire, yet the plan is to extend it**
**Where:** ticket §Produces, `ClaudeAccountErrorReason` — "`Schema.Literals([...])` with the 17 existing reasons"; §Test specification, "including ones that tickets 2 and 3 will add"

# Ticket 1 — Claude accounts over the wire: list, remember, forget — Round 2

### Blocked by
—

### Description
The server can already remember, list and forget Claude accounts (`ClaudeAccounts` in `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts`), but no client can reach it. This ticket makes those three operations callable over T3's WebSocket RPC, from the web and desktop app, locally and remotely. It moves the account schemas and the account error into `packages/contracts`. It rewrites the error messages that these three operations can return in plain words, with no internal setup ID and no command line in them. Later tickets build the screens on this.

No screen changes in this ticket. Switching (ticket 2) and adding an account (ticket 3) come later.

### Acceptance criteria
Scenario AK-14: Remembering the logged-in account from the Claude provider settings
  Given a Claude setup logged in with an account T3 has not remembered yet
  When the user chooses to remember it in the Claude provider settings and names it "Work"
  Then the account is remembered as "Work"
  And the settings list "Work" as the active account
Serves: R6

Scenario AK-25: Settings list the remembered accounts and mark the active one
  Given a Claude setup logged in as "Work" with "Work" and "Private" remembered
  When the user opens the Claude provider settings
  Then they see "Work" and "Private" listed
  And "Work" is marked as active
Serves: R10

Scenario AK-28: Confirming forget removes the account from the list
  Given the user has been asked to confirm forgetting "Private"
  When they confirm
  Then "Private" is no longer listed
  And "Private" is no longer offered for switching in the model picker
Serves: R10

Scenario AK-30: Forgetting the active account keeps the setup logged in
  Given a Claude setup logged in as the remembered account "Work"
  When the user forgets "Work" and confirms
  Then the setup is still logged in with that account
  And the account is shown as not remembered, with the offer to remember it
Serves: R10

Scenario AK-36: The desktop app connected remotely lists the remote setup's accounts
  Given the desktop app connected to a T3 on another machine whose Claude setup has "Work" active and "Private" remembered
  When the user opens the Claude provider settings
  Then they see "Work" and "Private" listed
  And "Work" is marked as active
Serves: R13

This ticket proves the server side of these scenarios, through the RPC boundary that a client uses. AK-36 is proven here only as far as AK-25 is. The remote connection itself is T3's generic environment transport, which no test in this repository drives end to end. The hand-off of ticket 4 names it as unproven.

This ticket also serves R11 for the refusals of list, remember and forget. AK-31 (refused switch) is proven in ticket 2 and AK-32 (refused add-account) in ticket 3. Those tickets rewrite the texts of their own reasons. The screens that show the result, the confirmation dialogs and the offer to remember come in ticket 4 (settings) and ticket 5 (model picker). They consume the RPCs defined here.

### Test specification
Unit (`packages/contracts/src/claudeAccounts.test.ts`, new):
- For each of the 9 reasons that list, remember and forget can return (`unavailable`, `setupNotFound`, `setupUnreadable`, `notLoggedIn`, `invalidName`, `nameInUse`, `alreadyRemembered`, `accountNotFound`, `storage`), a `ClaudeAccountError` built with `instanceId: "claudeAgent_work"` and `name: "Work"` has a non-empty `message`. The message contains none of: `claudeAgent_work`, a backtick, `claude auth`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. (Proves the plain-language rule for these reasons. Tickets 2 and 3 extend the list with the reasons they rewrite.)
- A `ClaudeAccountError({ reason: "nameInUse", name: "Work" })` that is encoded with `Schema.encodeUnknownSync(ClaudeAccountError)` and decoded again with `Schema.decodeUnknownSync(ClaudeAccountError)` keeps its `reason`, its `name` and the same `message`. This shows the client rebuilds the same text.
- Every literal in `ClaudeAccountErrorReason` round-trips through `Schema.encodeUnknownSync` and `Schema.decodeUnknownSync` of `ClaudeAccountError` three ways: with neither `name` nor `instanceId`, with only `name: "Work"`, and with only `instanceId: "claudeAgent"`. Each keeps its `reason` and its `message`.
- A `ClaudeAccountList` value round-trips unchanged through its schema. The value has two accounts and two setups, one with `active: null` and one with `active: { email, rememberedAs: null }`.

Integration (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts`, new `describe("over the WebSocket RPC")` that reuses the file's existing harness: temp setup dirs, real `ServerSecretStore`, pinned `HostProcess`). The RPCs run through `RpcServer.makeNoSerialization` over `RpcGroup.make(WsClaudeAccountsListRpc, WsClaudeAccountsRememberRpc, WsClaudeAccountsForgetRpc)`, with handlers from `claudeAccountsRpcHandlers` and the real `ClaudeAccounts` layer, the same way `apps/server/src/ws.test.ts:602-631` drives Rpcs:

- AK-28: after `claudeAccounts.forget { name: "Private" }`, `claudeAccounts.list` no longer contains "Private" in `accounts`.
- AK-30: after `claudeAccounts.forget { name: "Work" }` while Work is active, the setup's `.credentials.json` and `.claude.json` are byte-identical to before. `claudeAccounts.list` shows the setup with `active.email` unchanged and `active.rememberedAs === null`.

With `HostProcess.Platform` set to `"darwin"`, `claudeAccounts.list` fails with reason `unavailable`.

This is the permission behaviour test AGENTS.md:153 asks for when a protected method is added.

Existing tests that must keep passing unchanged in their assertions: the rest of `RpcAuthorization.test.ts` (one scope per Rpc) and `apps/server/src/ws.test.ts`. `ws.test.ts` gains one `Layer.mock(ClaudeAccounts.ClaudeAccounts)({})` entry in its mock wall, because `layerWsRpc` now yields the service. This ticket changes no existing assertion in `ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts`. The texts it pins at `:1374` and `:2214` belong to switch reasons, and ticket 2 changes them.

Boundaries doubled: the Claude login check (`ClaudeLoginCheck`, already scripted in the harness), the `/proc` scan (fake proc root, already in the harness) and the host process (`HostProcess.*`, pinned). Everything else is real: secret store, settings service, SQLite in memory, the RPC server.

# Ticket 2 — Switch Claude accounts over the wire: confirm gate, one switch at a time, fresh account display — Round 1

### Blocked by
#10

### Description
The server can already switch a Claude setup to another remembered account (`ClaudeAccounts.switch` in `apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.ts`), but no client can reach it. Today it also stops running turns without asking, queues a second switch instead of refusing it, and leaves the old account's email and usage in the provider snapshot for up to 5 minutes. This ticket makes the switch callable over T3's WebSocket RPC (`claudeAccounts.switch`) from the web and desktop app, locally and remotely, and makes it safe to call from a screen:

- If turns are running on the setup, the switch is refused with the reason `turnsRunning` before anything is stopped, unless the caller says `stopRunningTurns: true`. A screen asks the user, then calls again with `true`.
- While a switch runs, another switch is refused with the reason `switchInProgress`. It does not wait.
- After a successful switch, the provider snapshot of every affected setup is probed fresh, so every place that shows the Claude account or its usage shows the new account.
- Every refusal a switch can return reads in plain words, with no internal setup ID and no command line.

No screen changes in this ticket. The settings screen (ticket 4) and the model picker (ticket 5) call this RPC.

Decisions:
- The confirm gate is enforced on the server (`turnsRunning` unless `stopRunningTurns: true`), not by a client-side check of running threads. The client's thread shells match a thread's current instance selection, while the switch stops runs by the run's own instance. A client check could miss a turn and stop it without asking. What this gives up: an extra round trip before the confirmation dialog appears.
- The gate runs after the external-programs check and before the login check, which can take about 29 s. The user is asked quickly, and a switch that would be refused anyway does not ask first. What this gives up: a turn that starts during the login check of an already confirmed or turn-free switch is stopped without a second question. By then the user has chosen to switch, and the switch shows as in progress.
- A second switch is refused (`switchInProgress`) instead of queued, with one server-wide permit. All switches already serialise on `accountsLock`, so a per-setup permit would only let a second setup's switch wait behind the first, without asking. What this gives up: two different setups cannot be switched at the same moment. They can be switched one after the other.
- The provider refresh runs in the RPC handler module, not in `ClaudeAccounts`. The service would otherwise depend on `ProviderRegistry` and `ProviderInstanceRegistry`, which the account harness does not build. What this gives up: a server-side caller of `ClaudeAccounts.switch` other than the RPC must refresh itself. There is none today.

### Description

- Every refusal a switch can return reads in plain words, with no internal setup ID and no command line.

- `needsFreshLogin`: `The saved login of "${this.name}" no longer works. Forget "${this.name}", then add the account again.`
- `loginCheckFailed`: `Could not check the saved login of "${this.name}". Try again.` (unchanged)
- `switchFailed`: "Switching this Claude setup failed. It is still logged in as before."
- `switchRollbackFailed`: "Switching this Claude setup failed, and its previous login could not be restored. Log in to Claude again on this setup."
- `externalClaudePrograms`: "Claude programs started outside T3 are using this Claude setup. Close them, then switch again."
- `processCheckFailed`: "Could not check whether Claude programs outside T3 are using this Claude setup. Try again."
- `sessionStopFailed`: "Could not check or stop the running turns on this Claude setup. It is still logged in as before. Try again."
- `turnsRunning`: "Turns are running on this Claude setup. Switching the account stops them."
- `switchInProgress`: "Another Claude account switch is still running. Wait until it finishes, then try again."

Decisions:
- The confirmation gate is enforced on the server (`turnsRunning` unless `stopRunningTurns: true`), not by a client-side check of running threads.
  - Why: the client's thread shells match a thread's current instance selection, while the switch stops runs by the run's own instance. A client-side check could miss a turn and stop it without asking.
  - What this gives up: an extra round trip before the confirmation dialog appears.
- The gate runs twice: once before the login check, for a quick answer, and once right before the stop, for correctness.
  - Why: a single gate before the ~29 s check would let a turn that starts during the check be stopped without asking.
  - What this gives up: one extra projection read per switch that has no running turns. A turn that starts in the milliseconds between the second check and the stop's first pass is still stopped. That window is the stop step itself.
- A second switch is refused (`switchInProgress`) instead of queued, with one server-wide permit.
  - Why: all switches already serialise on `accountsLock`, so a per-setup permit would only let a second setup's switch wait behind the first, without asking.
  - What this gives up: two different setups cannot be switched at the same moment. They can be switched one after the other.
  - The permit is in-memory. One T3 server process owns its state dir, the remembered accounts in its secret store and its Claude setups. A second server process on the same state dir is not a supported setup, and nothing here guards it.
- The switch runs in the service layer's scope, and the caller only joins it.
  - Why: once turns are stopped, cutting the switch short would leave a setup that is half switched, or turns stopped for nothing, with no rollback. Until now no client could reach the switch, so this did not matter.
  - What this gives up: a caller cannot cancel a running switch. The switch is bounded by the login check and the 10 s stop timeout, so it ends on its own.
- The client command is single-flight per `[environmentId, input]`, as `startProviderAuth` is.
  - Why: a double click returns the first call's result, not a `switchInProgress` refusal. Different targets or other clients still reach the server and are refused there.
  - What this gives up: nothing beyond the precedent.

Consumers updated by the contracts change: `apps/server` (service, handler, scope map through the spread, instrumentation map) and `packages/client-runtime` (command and permission test). `apps/web`, `apps/desktop` and `apps/mobile` need no change, because `RpcClient.make(WsRpcGroup)` picks up the new tag.

Deliberately left out:
- Every screen (tickets 4 and 5), and adding an account (ticket 3).

- No docs change: `docs/internals/providers.md:52-69` already describes the stop-then-switch behaviour, and the confirmation is a client flow on top of it.

# Ticket 3 — Add a Claude account beside the setup: login in a throwaway folder — Round 1

### Blocked by
#10, #11

### Description
Today a user who wants a second Claude account on a setup has to log the setup out and log in again, and that loses the current login. This ticket adds an account **beside** the setup, on the server and over the wire. The setup's own login is never touched.

1. The client starts an attempt with the setup and a name, for example `{ instanceId: "claudeAgent", name: "Private" }`. The server checks the name first, so nobody logs in for nothing.
2. The server makes a fresh, private folder for this attempt. It runs the Claude CLI's own login, `claude auth login`, in a terminal (PTY) with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` pointing at that folder.
3. The terminal's output is streamed to the client that started the attempt. The client's keystrokes go back into the terminal. The CLI shows a login link. When the browser runs on another device, the login page there gives a code, and the user pastes it into this terminal.
4. When the CLI exits successfully, the server reads the new login from the folder and remembers it under the name, exactly as `remember` does. Then it deletes the folder.
5. If the attempt is cancelled, times out after 5 minutes, fails, or the client's connection closes, the server stops the CLI and deletes the folder. Nothing is remembered. When the server starts, it deletes every attempt folder an earlier run left behind.

Every refusal and failure reads in plain words. No screen changes in this ticket. The settings screen (ticket 4), the model picker (ticket 5) and the "Add provider" dialog (ticket 6) start an attempt through these RPCs and show its terminal.

What `make` does:
1. **Startup sweep (AK-24).** `loginsDir = path.join(serverConfig.stateDir, LOGINS_DIR_NAME)`. It runs `fileSystem.remove(loginsDir, { recursive: true, force: true })`, then `makeDirectory(loginsDir, { recursive: true })`, then `chmod(loginsDir, 0o700)`.
   - No attempt exists yet when the service starts, so everything in that folder was left by an earlier run.
   - If any of the three steps fails, `make` logs `Effect.logWarning("Claude account login folder could not be prepared", { operation: "addAccount", outcome: "sweepFailed" })` and continues. The server must start anyway. A `start` that then cannot make its own folder fails with `loginFailed`.
2. **State.** A `Map<string, Attempt>` where `Attempt = { id, owner, instanceId, name, fiber, state: SubscriptionRef<ClaudeAccountAddState>, write: (data) => void, resize: (cols, rows) => void }`.

`openConnection`:
- It makes `owner = yield* crypto.randomUUIDv4()`.
- It registers `Effect.addFinalizer(() => cancelAllOwnedBy(owner))`. This interrupts the fiber of every running attempt of that owner, and then removes every attempt record of that owner from the map.
- It returns the connection below.
- `lookup(owner, attemptId)` fails with `loginNotFound` (with `instanceId` omitted) when there is no record or `record.owner !== owner`. Another connection therefore cannot see whether an attempt exists.

`start(input)`:
1. `target = yield* accounts.prepareAddAccount(input)`.
2. `attemptId = yield* crypto.randomUUIDv4()`, and `dir = path.join(loginsDir, attemptId)`.
3. It forks `runAttempt` with `Effect.forkIn(layerScope)`. The attempt therefore outlives the RPC call, and ends only by itself, by cancel, by timeout, or by its owner's connection closing.
4. It waits on a `Deferred` that `runAttempt` completes once the PTY is spawned. If the folder or the spawn fails, the `Deferred` fails with `loginFailed`, and so does `start`.
5. It returns the first state: `phase: "running"`, `output: ""`, `outputOffset: 0`, `account: null`, `error: null`.

`runAttempt` is `Effect.scoped`:
1. `Effect.acquireRelease`: `makeDirectory(dir)`, then `chmod(dir, 0o700)`. The release is `fileSystem.remove(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })`, which logs a warning on failure and never fails.
2. `const env = yield* makeClaudeEnvironment({ homePath: dir }, target.environment)`. This sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=dir` and the owner-pid marker.
3. `Effect.acquireRelease`: `pty.spawn({ shell: target.binaryPath, args: ["auth", "login"], cwd: dir, cols: 80, rows: 24, env })`. The release detaches the listeners and calls `process.kill()` inside `try`, as `packages/provider-acp-registry/src/server/auth.ts:180-189` does.
4. `onData` appends to the transcript, keeps its last 16384 characters, adds the chunk length to `outputOffset`, and updates the state. The chunks pass through a sliding `Queue` of 64, as the ACP code does.
5. It waits for `onExit`'s `exitCode`, raced with `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_LOGIN_TIMEOUT` through `Effect.timeoutOrElse`. On timeout it fails with `loginTimedOut`.
6. If the exit code is not 0, it fails with `loginFailed`.
7. `login = yield* readClaudeSetupLogin({ configDir: dir, accountConfigPath: path.join(dir, ".claude.json") })`. If the read fails or returns `Option.none()`, it fails with `loginFailed`.
8. `account = yield* accounts.rememberLogin({ instanceId: target.instanceId, name: target.name, login: login.value })`.
9. The scope closes: the PTY is killed and the folder is removed. Only then is the final state published:
   - `succeeded` with `account`, or
   - `failed` with the `ClaudeAccountError`. Any other failure becomes `loginFailed`, and no cause is kept, because it could quote a login.
   - On interruption, `cancelled` is published by `cancel` (below), not by the fiber.

`respond`: `lookup`. If the attempt is no longer `running`, it fails `loginNotFound`. Otherwise it calls `resize(cols, rows)` when `size` is given, then `write(data)`. A throw from the PTY becomes `loginNotFound`.

`cancel`: `lookup`, then `Fiber.interrupt(attempt.fiber)`. That returns only after the finalizers ran, so the folder is gone and the PTY killed. Then it sets the state to `cancelled` if it is still `running`, and removes the record from the map. Cancelling an attempt that has already ended just removes its record and succeeds.

`subscribe`: `lookup`, then `SubscriptionRef.changes(attempt.state)` until and including the first state whose phase is not `running` (`Stream.takeUntil`). An ended attempt's record stays in the map until its owner cancels it or the connection closes. A subscriber that arrives after the end therefore still gets the final state.

Logs: `Effect.logInfo("Claude account login finished", { operation: "addAccount", outcome: <phase or reason>, instanceId, name })`. The terminal output, the folder path's contents and the login are never logged.

Decisions:
- **A dedicated attempt service, not `ProviderAuthFlow` or `provider.auth.*`.**
  - Why: `ProviderAuthFlow` is a provider's own sign-in controller. It replaces the instance's credentials and stops its sessions (`ProviderAuthService.ts:94-172`). This login must leave the setup and its running turns alone.
  - What this gives up: about 150 lines that look like `ProviderAuthFlow`'s attempt tracking. The terminal handling follows the ACP code closely.
- **The Claude CLI's own `claude auth login` in a PTY, not T3's own OAuth.**
  - Why: Claude's OAuth client and its redirect are the CLI's, and the CLI already writes exactly the files that `readClaudeSetupLogin` reads. A terminal lets the user paste the code that the login page shows when the browser is on another device (R7).
  - What this gives up: T3 depends on the CLI's interactive login. A change in its prompts shows up in the terminal, not as a typed error. Whether the code paste works from another device is not proven by a test.
- **The attempt folder lives under the state dir, not the OS temp dir.**
  - Why: a fixed parent is what makes the startup sweep possible (AK-24). The OS temp dir is shared and is not swept (`ClaudeLoginCheck`).
  - What this gives up: an attempt's login sits in the state dir for as long as the CLI runs, at mode 0700 like the secret store.
- **An attempt belongs to one WebSocket connection, not to an auth session.**
  - Why: "close the app without cancelling" must delete the login (AK-23), and a closed socket is the only sign of that. An auth session survives closing the app.
  - What this gives up: a dropped connection loses the attempt, and the user starts again.
- **The name is asked before the login and checked again after it.**
  - Why: a name that is taken is refused before anyone logs in. The second check under `accountsLock` covers a name taken in the meantime.
  - What this gives up: the screen asks for the name first. The mocks already show it this way.
- **No limit on parallel attempts.** Each attempt has its own folder and process, and remembering is serialised by `accountsLock`.
  - What this gives up: a client could start many attempts. Each needs `providers:manage` and ends within 5 minutes.

Consumers updated by the contracts change: `apps/server` (handlers, scope map, instrumentation map) and `packages/client-runtime` (atoms and the permission test). `apps/web`, `apps/desktop` and `apps/mobile` need no change in this ticket, because `RpcClient.make(WsRpcGroup)` picks up the new tags.

# Ticket 3 — Add a Claude account beside the setup: login in a throwaway folder — Round 1

### Blocked by
#10, #11

### Description
Today a user who wants a second Claude account on a setup has to log the setup out and log in again, and that loses the current login. This ticket adds an account **beside** the setup, on the server and over the wire. The setup's own login is never touched.

1. The client starts an attempt with the setup and a name, for example `{ instanceId: "claudeAgent", name: "Private" }`. The server checks the name first, so nobody logs in for nothing.
2. The server makes a fresh, private folder for this attempt. It runs the Claude CLI's own login, `claude auth login`, in a terminal (PTY) with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` pointing at that folder.
3. The terminal's output is streamed to the client that started the attempt. The client's keystrokes go back into the terminal. The CLI shows a login link. When the browser runs on another device, the login page there gives a code, and the user pastes it into this terminal.
4. When the CLI exits successfully, the server reads the new login from the folder and remembers it under the name, exactly as `remember` does. Then it deletes the folder.
5. If the attempt is cancelled, times out after 5 minutes, fails, or the client's connection closes before the CLI has exited successfully, the server stops the CLI and deletes the folder. Nothing is remembered. Once the CLI has exited successfully, remembering runs to its end and the attempt reports its true outcome. When the server starts, it deletes every attempt folder an earlier run left behind.
6. One connection runs at most one attempt. Starting a new one cancels the connection's previous attempt first.

Every refusal and failure reads in plain words. No screen changes in this ticket. The settings screen (ticket 4), the model picker (ticket 5) and the "Add provider" dialog (ticket 6) start an attempt through these RPCs and show its terminal.

### Acceptance criteria
Scenario AK-15: Adding an account keeps the setup logged in
  Given a Claude setup logged in as the remembered account "Work"
  When the user adds another account, logs in with it in the browser and names it "Private"
  Then "Private" is remembered
  And the setup is still logged in as "Work"
Serves: R7

Scenario AK-16: Adding an account works when the browser is on another device
  Given T3 runs on one machine and the user's browser runs on a different device
  And a Claude setup logged in as the remembered account "Work"
  When the user adds another account, completes the login in that browser and names it "Private"
  Then "Private" is remembered
  And the setup is still logged in as "Work"
Serves: R7

Scenario AK-22: Cancelling the add-account login leaves no login behind
  Given the user has started adding an account and has not finished the login
  When they cancel
  Then no new account is remembered
  And no login for that attempt remains on the machine
Serves: R9

Scenario AK-23: Closing the add-account step without finishing leaves no login behind
  Given the user has started adding an account
  When they close the dialog or the app without cancelling
  Then no new account is remembered
  And no login for that attempt remains on the machine
Serves: R9

Scenario AK-24: An add-account attempt interrupted by a T3 restart leaves no login behind
  Given the user has started adding an account and has not finished the login
  When T3 restarts
  Then no login for that attempt remains on the machine once T3 is running again
Serves: R9

Scenario AK-32: A refused add-account tells the user why in plain words
  Given the user is adding an account and the login fails or is refused
  When T3 reports the failure
  Then the user sees a plain-language reason that names no internal identifiers or commands
  And no new account is remembered
Serves: R11

This ticket proves the server side of these scenarios at the service and RPC boundary that a client uses.

- AK-16: the tests prove that the client's keystrokes (a pasted code) and terminal size reach the login terminal, and that the result does not depend on where the browser runs. No test runs the real `claude auth login`. The guard rails forbid touching a real Claude login, and the CLI needs a real browser login. Whether the real CLI accepts a pasted code from another device is **unproven by any automated test in this Auftrag**. It stays unproven until a manual check: the hand-off of ticket 4, the first ticket with a screen that starts an add, asks the human to add an account once from a browser on another device before the Auftrag is closed.
- AK-23: "close the dialog" is the screen calling `cancel` on unmount. Each of tickets 4, 5 and 6 has its own add-account screen, and each proves the dialog-close half for its own screen. "Close the app" is the WebSocket connection closing, proven here.

### Test specification
Unit (`packages/contracts/src/claudeAccounts.test.ts`, extends the cases of tickets 1 and 2):
- The plain-language case now covers all 22 reasons, including `loginFailed`, `loginTimedOut` and `loginNotFound`. For each, a `ClaudeAccountError` built with `instanceId: "claudeAgent_work"` and `name: "Work"` has a non-empty `message` that contains none of: `claudeAgent_work`, a backtick, `claude auth`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.
- A `ClaudeAccountAddState` with `phase: "failed"` and `error: new ClaudeAccountError({ reason: "nameInUse", name: "Private" })` round-trips through `Schema.encodeUnknownSync` and `Schema.decodeUnknownSync`, keeping `error.reason` and `error.message`.
- `ClaudeAccountAddRespondInput` refuses `data` of 4097 characters, and refuses `size: { cols: 0, rows: 24 }`.
- `ProviderAuthResponse` still decodes `{ type: "terminal", data: "x", size: { cols: 80, rows: 24 } }` after its terminal member is extracted into `ProviderAuthTerminalResponse`.

Unit (`packages/client-runtime/src/state/commandPermissions.test.ts`, one new case shaped like the one at `:93-117`):
- `createCommandPermissions(runtime, WS_METHODS.claudeAccountsAddStart)`: a session without `AuthProvidersManageScope` gives `permissionAtom(env) === false` and `authorize` fails with `EnvironmentAuthorizationError`. A session with it gives `true`, and `authorize` succeeds. Another environment's grant does not leak.

Unit (`apps/server/src/auth/RpcAuthorization.test.ts`, extends ticket 1's scope case):
- `requiredScopeForRpcMethod` of `claudeAccountsAddStart`, `claudeAccountsAddRespond`, `claudeAccountsAddCancel` and `claudeAccountsAddSubscribe` is each `AuthProvidersManageScope`.

Integration (`apps/server/src/provider/ClaudeAccounts.integration.test.ts`, new `describe("adding an account beside the setup")`):

Harness changes:
- `makeAccountsTestLayer` provideMerges `ClaudeAccountLoginModule.layer` over the accounts layer. It provides `Layer.succeed(PtyAdapter.PtyAdapter, fakePty)`, where `fakePty` is a new local `FakeLoginPty`. The harness exposes it as `h.pty` and the service as `h.login`.
- `FakeLoginPty` is a small local fake modelled on `FakePtyAdapter` and `FakePtyProcess` in `apps/server/src/terminal/Manager.test.ts:76-175`. Those are not exported, so it is not imported from there. It records `spawnInputs`, `writes`, `resizeCalls` and `killed`, and offers `emitData(text)`, `emitExit(exitCode)` and `failNextSpawn()`, which makes the next `spawn` fail with `PtySpawnError`.

- Each case opens a connection with `const connection = yield* h.login.openConnection` inside a child `Scope`, so the test can close that scope to stand in for a closed WebSocket.
- "The login" in these tests: after `start`, the test calls the existing `writeLoginFiles(h.pty.spawnInputs[0].env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, carol)` (`:146`), adds the tokens it returns to `h.tokens`, then calls `h.pty.emitExit(0)`.
- To wait for the end of an attempt, the test runs `connection.subscribe({ attemptId })` until the first state whose `phase` is not `"running"` (`Stream.takeUntil`, `Stream.runLast`). There are no sleeps and no polling.

Cases (setup `claudeAgent` logged in as `alice`, remembered as "Work", unless a case says otherwise):
- AK-15: `start({ instanceId: "claudeAgent", name: "Private" })` returns `phase: "running"`. Then:
  - The spawn input is `shell: "claude"` and `args: ["auth", "login"]`.
  - Its `env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is a folder directly under `${h.stateDir}/claude-account-logins/`, with mode `0o700`.
  - Its `env.T3CODE_CLAUDE_OWNER_PID` is `"4242"`.
  - After "the login", the final state is `phase: "succeeded"` and `account: { name: "Private", email: carol.email }`.
  - `h.accounts.list` contains "Private", and the setup's `active.rememberedAs` is still `"Work"`.

Contract for the screens (tickets 4–6):
- Show "Add account…" only when `serverEnvironment.startClaudeAccountAdd.permissionAtom(environmentId)` is true and the environment's `platform.os === "linux"`.
- Ask for the name first, then call `startClaudeAccountAdd`. A refusal (`invalidName`, `nameInUse`, `unavailable`) comes back before any login starts. Show its `message`.
- Subscribe with `claudeAccountAddState({ environmentId, input: { attemptId } })`. Render `output` and `outputOffset` with `ProviderAuthTerminal`, and send its responses through `respondClaudeAccountAdd` without `type`.
- On `succeeded`, refresh `claudeAccountList` (ticket 1's refresh contract). On `failed`, show `error.message` in the usual error style.
- When the user cancels, or the add-account step unmounts while the state is `running`, call `cancelClaudeAccountAdd`.
- An attempt belongs to the WebSocket connection that started it. If the connection drops while the attempt is `running`, the attempt is gone, and the re-subscription gives `loginNotFound`, whose text tells the user to start again. A final state already shown stays, because the subscription has ended.
- One add at a time per client connection: starting a second one cancels the first.

- `loginFailed`: "The Claude login did not finish, so no account was added. Try again."
- `loginTimedOut`: "The Claude login took longer than 5 minutes and was stopped. No account was added. Start again."
- `loginNotFound`: "This Claude login is no longer running. Start adding the account again."
- `nameInUse`, `invalidName`, `alreadyRemembered`, `unavailable`, `setupNotFound` and `setupUnreadable` keep ticket 1's texts.

What `make` does:
1. **Startup sweep (AK-24).** `loginsDir = path.join(serverConfig.stateDir, LOGINS_DIR_NAME)`. It runs `fileSystem.remove(loginsDir, { recursive: true, force: true })` on every platform. Only when `yield* HostProcess.Platform` is `"linux"` does it then run `makeDirectory(loginsDir, { recursive: true })` and `chmod(loginsDir, 0o700)`. Elsewhere the feature cannot run, and `start` refuses with `unavailable` through `prepareAddAccount`.
   - No attempt exists yet when the service starts, so everything in that folder was left by an earlier run.
   - If any step fails, `make` logs `Effect.logWarning("Claude account login folder could not be prepared", { operation: "addAccount", outcome: "sweepFailed" })` and continues. The server must start anyway. A `start` that then cannot make its own folder fails with `loginFailed`.
2. **State.** A `Map<string, Attempt>` where `Attempt = { id, owner, instanceId, name, fiber, state: SubscriptionRef<ClaudeAccountAddState>, write: (data) => void, resize: (cols, rows) => void }`. Map changes and the steps named below run under one `Semaphore.make(1)` called `attemptsLock`.

`openConnection`:
- It makes `owner = yield* crypto.randomUUIDv4()` and a local `closed = false`.
- It registers `Effect.addFinalizer(() => closeOwner(owner))`. Under `attemptsLock`, this sets `closed = true` and takes every record of that owner out of the map. Outside the lock, it interrupts their fibers.
- It returns the connection below.
- `lookup(owner, attemptId)` fails with `loginNotFound` (with `instanceId` omitted) when there is no record or `record.owner !== owner`. Another connection therefore cannot see whether an attempt exists.

`start(input)`:
1. `target = yield* accounts.prepareAddAccount(input)`.
2. `attemptId = yield* crypto.randomUUIDv4()`, and `dir = path.join(loginsDir, attemptId)`.
3. Under `attemptsLock`, and uninterruptibly:
   - If `closed`, fail `loginNotFound`.
   - Otherwise take the owner's previous record, if any, out of the map.
   - Fork `runAttempt` with `Effect.forkIn(layerScope)`, and put the new record with its fiber into the map in the same step. The connection's finalizer therefore always finds the attempt.
   - The attempt outlives the RPC call. It ends only by itself, by cancel, by timeout, by a newer `start` on the same connection, or by its owner's connection closing.
4. Outside the lock, it interrupts the previous record's fiber, if there was one. This is the same as `cancel`.
5. It waits on a `Deferred` that `runAttempt` completes once the PTY is spawned. `runAttempt` is wrapped in `Effect.onExit`, which fails the `Deferred` with `loginFailed` on any exit before the spawn: a folder failure, a spawn failure, a defect or an interruption. `start` then fails with that, and its record is removed.
6. It returns the first state: `phase: "running"`, `output: ""`, `outputOffset: 0`, `account: null`, `error: null`.

`runAttempt` is `Effect.scoped`:
1. `Effect.acquireRelease`: `makeDirectory(dir)`, then `chmod(dir, 0o700)`. The release is `fileSystem.remove(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })`, which logs a warning on failure and never fails.
2. `const env = yield* makeClaudeEnvironment({ homePath: dir }, target.environment)`. This sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=dir` and the owner-pid marker.
3. `Effect.acquireRelease`: `pty.spawn({ shell: target.binaryPath, args: ["auth", "login"], cwd: dir, cols: 80, rows: 24, env })`. The release detaches the listeners and calls `process.kill()` inside `try`, as `packages/provider-acp-registry/src/server/auth.ts:180-189` does.
4. `onData` appends to the transcript, keeps its last 16384 characters, adds the chunk length to `outputOffset`, and updates the state. The chunks pass through a sliding `Queue` of 64, as the ACP code does.
5. It waits for `onExit`'s `exitCode`, raced with `CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_LOGIN_TIMEOUT` through `Effect.timeoutOrElse`. On timeout it fails with `loginTimedOut`.
6. If the exit code is not 0, it fails with `loginFailed`.
7. From here on, the attempt runs **uninterruptibly** (`Effect.uninterruptible` around steps 7–9). The CLI has exited 0, so the login exists. A cancel or a closed connection now waits for the true outcome instead of cutting it in half.
8. `const paths = yield* resolveClaudeSetupPaths({ homePath: dir }, env)`. This is the repository's one rule for where `.claude.json` sits. With `homePath` set, it gives `{ configDir: dir, accountConfigPath: <dir>/.claude.json }`.
   - `login = yield* readClaudeSetupLogin(paths)`. If the read fails or returns `Option.none()`, it fails with `loginFailed`.
   - `account = yield* accounts.rememberLogin({ instanceId: target.instanceId, name: target.name, login: login.value })`. This waits on `accountsLock` if a switch holds it. That wait is bounded only by the switch's own limits: its login check, and the 10 s stop timeout (`CLAUDE_SWITCH_STOP_TIMEOUT`). The 5-minute timeout does not cover it. Meanwhile the attempt stays `running` with an exited terminal.
9. The scope closes: the PTY is killed and the folder is removed. Only then is the final state published:
   - `succeeded` with `account`, or
   - `failed` with the `ClaudeAccountError`. Any other failure becomes `loginFailed`, and no cause is kept, because it could quote a login.
   - On interruption (only possible before step 7), `cancelled` is published by `cancel` (below), not by the fiber.

`respond`: `lookup`. If the attempt is no longer `running`, it fails `loginNotFound`. Otherwise it calls `resize(cols, rows)` when `size` is given, then `write(data)`. A throw from the PTY becomes `loginNotFound`.

`cancel`: `lookup`, then `Fiber.interrupt(attempt.fiber)`.
- That returns only after the fiber ended, so the folder is gone and the PTY killed.
- If the fiber was already past step 7, the interrupt waits for it, and the published final state (`succeeded` or `failed`) stands.
- Otherwise `cancel` sets the state to `cancelled`.
- Then it removes the record from the map. Cancelling an attempt that has already ended just removes its record and succeeds.

`subscribe`: `lookup`, then `SubscriptionRef.changes(attempt.state)` until and including the first state whose phase is not `running` (`Stream.takeUntil`). An ended attempt's record stays in the map until its owner cancels it, starts a newer attempt, or closes the connection. So each connection holds at most one record, and a subscriber that arrives after the end still gets the final state.

- Adding a Claude account runs `claude auth login` with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set to a fresh 0700 folder under `<stateDir>/claude-account-logins/`, through `makeClaudeEnvironment`, so it is marked and never touches a setup's own config dir.

Decisions:
- **A dedicated attempt service, not `ProviderAuthFlow` or `provider.auth.*`.**
  - Why: `ProviderAuthFlow` is a provider's own sign-in controller. It replaces the instance's credentials and stops its sessions (`ProviderAuthService.ts:94-172`). This login must leave the setup and its running turns alone.
  - What this gives up: about 150 lines that look like `ProviderAuthFlow`'s attempt tracking. The terminal handling follows the ACP code closely.
- **The Claude CLI's own `claude auth login` in a PTY, not T3's own OAuth.**
  - Why: Claude's OAuth client and its redirect are the CLI's, and the CLI already writes exactly the files that `readClaudeSetupLogin` reads. A terminal lets the user paste the code that the login page shows when the browser is on another device (R7).
  - What this gives up: T3 depends on the CLI's interactive login. A change in its prompts shows up in the terminal, not as a typed error. Whether the code paste works from another device is not proven by a test.
- **The attempt folder lives under the state dir, not the OS temp dir.**
  - Why: a fixed parent is what makes the startup sweep possible (AK-24). The OS temp dir is shared and is not swept (`ClaudeLoginCheck`).
  - What this gives up: an attempt's login sits in the state dir for as long as the CLI runs, at mode 0700 like the secret store.
- **An attempt belongs to one WebSocket connection, not to an auth session.**
  - Why: "close the app without cancelling" must delete the login (AK-23), and a closed socket is the only sign of that. An auth session survives closing the app.
  - What this gives up: a dropped connection loses the attempt, and the user starts again.
- **The name is asked before the login and checked again after it.**
  - Why: a name that is taken is refused before anyone logs in. The second check under `accountsLock` covers a name taken in the meantime.
  - What this gives up: the screen asks for the name first. The mocks already show it this way.
- **One attempt per connection. A new `start` cancels the previous one.**
  - Why: one client adds one account at a time. This bounds CLI processes, login folders and kept records to one per connection.
  - What this gives up: one tab cannot run two logins side by side. Two tabs can.
- **Once the CLI exited 0, remembering is uninterruptible.**
  - Why: a cancel after the save must not report `cancelled` for an account that was remembered (AK-22).
  - What this gives up: a cancel at that moment waits for the remember. While a switch holds `accountsLock`, that can be as long as the switch takes.
- **The state embeds `ClaudeAccountError`, not a `message` string as `ProviderAuthState` does.**
  - Why: screens keep the machine-readable `reason` (for example to branch on `alreadyRemembered`), and the client rebuilds the same plain text from its own class (fact #37).
  - What this gives up: the add state differs from the sibling `ProviderAuthState` shape.
- **The terminal output may echo what the user types, including a pasted login code.**
  - Why that is acceptable: the code is a one-time code that the same user just typed on that client. The output goes only to the owner connection, lives in memory only while the record exists, and is never logged. `ProviderSetupError`'s rule against OAuth codes concerns error texts, and no error text here contains output.

Consumers updated by the contracts change: `apps/server` (handlers, scope map, instrumentation map) and `packages/client-runtime` (atoms and the permission test). `apps/web`, `apps/desktop` and `apps/mobile` need no change in this ticket, because `RpcClient.make(WsRpcGroup)` picks up the new tags. The `ProviderAuthTerminalResponse` extraction keeps `ProviderAuthResponse`'s type identical, so its consumers (`ProviderAuthTerminal`, `ProviderAuthenticationSection`, the ACP registry auth) compile unchanged.

The client atoms land here, not in ticket 4, because tickets 4, 5 and 6 all start an add. Landing them once with their RPCs keeps the wire contract and its client in one reviewed place, as tickets 1 and 2 do.

Deliberately left out:
- Every screen (tickets 4–6).
- A typed "open this link" interaction parsed from the CLI's output. The terminal shows the link as the CLI prints it.
- Logging the setup out, or switching to the new account. Adding never changes the setup.
- Surviving a reconnect.

# Ticket 4 — Claude provider settings: remembered accounts, switch, forget, remember, add — Round 1

### Blocked by
#10, #11, #13

### Description
Tickets 1–3 made the Claude account operations callable over the wire. No screen uses them yet. This ticket adds them to the Claude provider card in Settings → Providers, on Linux only:

1. **Account row** ("Claude account"). It shows which account is logged in on this Claude setup, and that the account is used by all chats on the setup. If T3 has not remembered that account yet, the row offers "Remember…", which asks for a name.
2. **Remembered accounts.** Every remembered account is listed with its email. The account that is logged in on this setup is marked "Active". Every other account has "Switch". Every account has "Forget", which asks for confirmation first. "Add account…" opens a dialog: the user names the new account, then logs in with it in a terminal inside the dialog. The browser can run on another device. In that case the user pastes the code shown by the login page into the terminal.
3. **Switching.** A switch starts at once when no turns run on the setup. If turns run, the user first confirms that they will be stopped. While a switch runs, the card shows that it is in progress, and no second switch can be started from this card or from the model picker (ticket 5).
4. **Refusals.** Every refusal shows the server's own plain-language message in the usual inline error style.

The card shows none of this when T3 does not run on Linux, or when the session may not manage providers.

This ticket also produces the web pieces that the model picker (ticket 5) and the "Add provider" dialog (ticket 6) reuse: the availability check, the account query, the switch flow with its shared in-progress state, the remember dialog and the add-account login step.

Forget flow: `confirm` first. On `true`, `forgetClaudeAccount({ environmentId, input: { name } })`. On success, `refresh()`. On failure, the alert line shows `claudeAccountErrorMessage(failure)`. A ref guards against a double click, like `CodexSetupSection`'s `pendingRef` (`:327-353`).

`RememberClaudeAccountDialog`: `Dialog` + `WizardPopup` + `WizardHeader title="Remember this Claude account" description="Logged in as {email}.
